IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. This position is based in Dakar, Senegal as part of Regional Supply Chain office for Africa. Depending on current and anticipated needs, it may require frequent deployments to support National Red Cross Societies as well as IFRC programmes and operations within the Region and Globally. The Supply Chain Senior Officer plays a strategic and operational role at the intersection of programmes and operations, ensuring that logistics and supply chain services enable timely, efficient, and accountable delivery of humanitarian assistance before, during, and after emergencies. The Supply Chain Senior Officer reports to the Head, Regional Supply Chain Management Unit for Africa based in Nairobi. Job Purpose The Regional Senior Supply Chain Officer provides regional technical leadership and operational support to ensure the timely, compliant, cost-effective, and reliable movement of humanitarian goods across Africa. Based in Dakar and working as part of the Regional Supply Chain Management Unit for Africa, with its regional presence in Dakar and Nairobi, the position serves as a focal point for air, sea and road transportation, international and regional freight forwarding, import and export processes, and customs facilitation for IFRC offices, operations, and Red Cross/Red Crescent National Societies. A central purpose of the role is to support the establishment, implementation, and performance management of regional framework agreements for air/sea and road transport, freight forwarding, customs clearance, and related logistics services. The position will also lead and maintain regional customs and corridor mapping, including country import requirements, exemptions, documentation, border crossings, ports and airports, clearance arrangements, transit constraints, and viable alternative routes. This work will strengthen preparedness, improve market coverage, reduce lead times and costs, and enable faster scale-up during emergencies. The senior officer provides hands-on support to resolve complex transportation, freight, and customs challenges affecting operations across the continent. This includes working with National Societies, government and customs authorities, clearing agents, transporters, freight forwarders, Movement partners, and other stakeholders to remove bottlenecks, address delayed or non-compliant shipments, and identify practical routing and delivery solutions. Be available for rapid deployment to establish/reinforce transportation, freight, and customs functions during emergencies and other periods of increased operational demand. Provide movement tracking, operational updates, risk analysis, and recommended actions to management and response teams during critical shipments and emergency scale-up. Lead/contribute to after-action reviews ensuring operational lessons are translated to improved agreements, procedures, corridor maps, and preparedness measures.
